name: Timing belt tensioner
what: The timing belt tensioner maintains the correct tension in the timing belt.
why: Correct belt tension helps prevent the belt from jumping teeth or running off its sprockets.
where: It mounts near the timing-belt path on the timing-belt end of the engine.
installationReason: Install the tensioner after the water pump and camshaft gears are in place. Its final adjustment must follow the correct B16 belt-tensioning procedure.

guide.overview: The timing belt tensioner controls slack in the belt that synchronizes the crankshaft and camshafts.
guide.operation: The tensioner pulley applies controlled force to the belt span. Correct tension helps maintain timing and limits belt vibration.
guide.construction: This educational procedural model shows a tensioner pulley, central bearing hub, mounting arm, and adjustment feature. It is not a factory CAD reproduction.
guide.specifications: Exact pulley diameter, spring force, adjustment position, belt deflection, and fastener torque depend on the specific B16 variant and service procedure.
guide.inspection: Inspect the pulley bearing for roughness or play and check the tensioner arm and spring for damage. Set belt tension using the matching Honda service manual.
guide.failureModes: A seized pulley, weak spring, incorrect adjustment, or worn bearing can cause belt noise, loss of tension, or timing-belt failure.
